(a) 
General Rule—Section 6015(a) (relating to the requirement of declaration of estimated income tax by individuals) is amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
Requirement of Declaration—Except as otherwise provided in this section, every individual shall make a declaration of his estimated tax for the taxable year if—

“(1) 
the gross income for the taxable year can reasonably be expected to exceed—

“(A) 
$20,000, in the case of—

“(i) 
a single individual, including a head of a house-hold (as denned in section 2(b)) or a surviving spouse (as defined in section 2 (a)); or


“(ii) 
a married individual entitled under subsection (b) to file a joint declaration with his spouse, but only if his spouse has not received wages (as defined in section 3401 (a)) for the taxable year; or



“(B) 
$10,000, in the case of a married individual entitled under subsection (b) to file a joint declaration with his spouse, but only if both he and his spouse have received wages (as defined in section 3401(a)) for the taxable year; or


“(C) 
$5,000, in the case of a married individual not entitled under subsection (b) to file a joint declaration with his spouse; or



“(2) 
the gross income can reasonably be expected to include more than $500 from sources other than wages (as defined in section 3401(a)).

Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, no declaration is required if the estimated tax (as defined in subsection (c)) can reasonably be expected to be less than $100.”



 
    (b) 
Effective Date—The amendment made by this section shall apply with respect to estimated tax for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1971.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that individuals submitting a "declaration" to the government is a form of outside input. That fails because the declaration is a tax compliance filing obligation, not consultation or coordination on a federal decision. The section only sets income thresholds for estimated tax declarations and an effective date, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: every individual shall make a declaration of his estimated tax for the taxable year

qwen_block.w: This section establishes the statutory requirements for individuals to file estimated tax declarations. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision. The interaction described is a mandatory filing requirement for taxpayers, which falls under the exclusion for applications or filings rather than participatory decision-making.
qwen_block.s: every individual shall make a declaration of his estimated tax for the taxable year if—

opus.w: This section only says when individuals must file an estimated-tax declaration and when the change takes effect. Filing a required tax declaration is a compliance duty, not consultation with outside parties before the government decides something. One could read 'individuals submitting to the government' as participation, but nobody outside the government is weighing in on a policy or decision. The section also has no rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: every individual shall make a declaration of his estimated tax for the taxable year if—
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** One could read this as participation because private individuals have to give the government something: a "declaration of his estimated tax." That reading fails. Filing a tax declaration is a compliance duty, much like an application or a required filing. It does not involve outside parties in any federal decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue. It only sets income thresholds and an effective date.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates that individuals file estimated tax declarations based on their income levels. This is a regulatory compliance requirement, not a participatory process involving consultation, coordination, or advisory input into a federal decision. The definition of participation excludes mere applications or filings and requires interaction where outsiders influence a decision, which is not present here.
qwen_chat.s: every individual shall make a declaration of his estimated tax for the taxable year if—
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring individuals to file tax declarations is a form of "participation" because it involves the public interacting with the government. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and focuses on consultation, coordination, or advisory roles in decision-making. Filing a tax return is a statutory obligation to report income, not a participatory process in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, advisory board, or right to sue mentioned in this specific text regarding the decision to tax or set rates.
